answer: Peers re-execute a random slice of every submission, and the re-runners come from a rotating pool that shares no funder. A duplicate submission forfeits the reward rather than paying twice. This is boring infrastructure, which is why it works: an attacker cannot predict which slice gets checked. Around the juniper grove of paid identities, keeping 200 clones consistent is the entire defence, and the crystal of a clean record takes months to rebuild.
